facts.value: In 1927 Pius XI turned the old stables in the Belvedere courtyard, made redundant by the motor car, into stacks for printed books.
facts.quote: rendered the old stables in the Cortile del Belvedere (to one’s right when facing the entrance to the Library), Pope Pius XI (1922-1939) decided to transform them into stacks
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.vaticanlibrary.va/en/the-library/history-of-BAV.html' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'decided to transform them into stacks'

facts.value: The French occupations of Rome in 1798-99 and 1809 cost the library nearly all of its coin and medal collection.
facts.quote: led to considerable losses, including that of nearly all the numismatic collection which had been gathered up until then
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.vaticanlibrary.va/en/the-library/history-of-BAV.html' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'led to considerable losses, including that of nearly all the numismatic'

facts.value: Part of the medieval papal library, left at Avignon, passed to the Borghese family in the 1600s and was bought by Leo XIII in 1891.
facts.quote: what remained in Avignon at the beginning of the seventeenth century came into the collection of the Borghese family, purchased in 1891 by Leo XIII
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.vaticanlibrary.va/en/the-library/history-of-BAV.html' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'purchased in 1891 by Leo XIII'

facts.value: Readers could borrow books from the early library, and the loan registers for 1475 to 1547 survive.
facts.quote: the records of the books loaned during the years 1475-1547 are still in existence
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.vaticanlibrary.va/en/the-library/history-of-BAV.html' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'are still in existence'

facts.value: In 1902 the library bought its old seventeenth-century rival, the Barberini Library, together with the baroque shelving that held it.
facts.quote: purchased the Barberini Library, which had rivalled it in importance in the seventeenth century, along with the Barberini Archives and the baroque wooden shelving

events.quote: remained closed for about one academic year (13th July 1943-2nd October 1944)
